title: Order Cancellation, Return, and Refund
readerIntent: Understand the complete governed order-aftercare capability, ownership boundaries, business outcomes, and implementation maturity.
owner: Order owns lifecycle intent; Fulfillment, Inventory, Payment, Product, Workflow, Notification, and KYC retain their domain authority
summary: Nodics supports full and partial cancellation, Return/RMA, and original-rail Refund as persisted, versioned, permissioned journeys with audit, notification, provider recovery, and customer customization.

sections.heading: What is Order Lifecycle Management?
items: It is the governed business capability for cancellation, Return/RMA and Refund after an order is placed.
Customers and support can request a full or partial cancellation with reason and immutable item scope.
Return operations can authorize multiple RMAs, receive serialized or bulk goods, inspect and disposition them, then expose refund eligibility.
Finance can calculate, approve and execute exact refunds on the original payment rails, including split payments, tax, shipping, discount and adjustment evidence.
Decision makers receive one governed aftercare model with configurable policy, explicit ownership, audit, recovery and provider portability.

sections.heading: Beginner mental model
items: Order owns what the customer or employee requested and its overall state.

Fulfillment owns shipment cancellation and physical Return/RMA. Inventory owns allocation release and disposition movement. Payment owns void, refund and provider reconciliation. Product owns entitlement revocation.
Workflow owns long-running review and maker-checker. Notification owns delivery after Order publishes bounded intent. Axis displays permission-filtered backend facts and actions.

sections.heading: Journeys
items: Cancellation: submit → evaluate owner evidence → calculate financial impact → approve → execute owners → complete or reconcile.
Return: submit → validate → authorize RMA → receive → inspect → disposition → calculate refund eligibility → complete or reconcile.
Refund: submit → exact calculation → risk and approval → maker-checker → original-rail provider execution → complete or reconcile.

sections.heading: Enterprise controls
items: Tenant and enterprise scope, record ownership, bounded input, rate limiting, idempotency, optimistic revision checks, immutable decision evidence, safe projections and append-only audit apply throughout.
Provider timeouts are uncertain outcomes, never automatic failures suitable for blind retry. Reconciliation must compare authoritative provider facts with the exact approved allocation.
Customer modules may layer configuration, services, Pipeline nodes, Workflow definitions, metadata and providers without editing core or bypassing an owner service.

sections.heading: Implementation and qualification
items: Persisted deterministic runtime journeys cover cancellation, Return/RMA and Refund across real owner services and configured Pipelines.
Axis has a dedicated Order Lifecycle Management presentation over backend-published workspaces.
A deployment must still qualify selected payment and carrier accounts, credentials, webhooks, regional controls, monitoring, load and disaster recovery in its target environment.
